title: Criteria for issuance of court or administrative order for treatment over the patient's objection.
bodyText:
[Part X.] ADMINISTRATION OF TREATMENT OVER THE PATIENT'S OBJECTION

(a) A patient who has been committed to a psychiatric facility for involuntary hospitalization or who is in the custody of the director and residing in a psychiatric facility may be ordered to receive treatment over the patient's objection, including the taking or application of medication, if the court, or administrative decision-maker through the administrative authorization process established pursuant to section 334-162, finds that:

(1) The patient suffers from a physical or mental disease, disorder, or defect;

(2) The patient is imminently dangerous to self or others;

(3) The proposed treatment is medically appropriate; and

(4) After considering less intrusive alternatives, treatment is necessary to forestall the danger posed by the patient.

(b) For the purposes of this section, "imminently dangerous to self or others" means that, without intervention, the person will likely become dangerous to self or dangerous to others within the next forty-five days.
